Julian, 52,000 tons of first-class ore averaging 20 ounces of silver and 0.08 ounce of gold to the ton.

Careful sampling of the outcrop showed it to be barren, except for a narrow streak against the wall of the old prospect shaft, which yielded, according to Super- intendent William Watters, 100 ounces of silver to the ton.
The vein is 6 inches thick and is reported to carry in places $40 a ton in gold.
